chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn al-Salt from Zur'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend to enter the state of Ihram on the Day of Tashriq (Day of Tarwiyah), do as you did when you intended to enter Ihram initially: trim your mustache, cut your nails, remove hair from your pubic area if you have hair there, pluck your armpits, perform Ghusl (ritual bath), and put on your Ihram garments. Then go to Al-Masjid Al-Haram and pray six Rak'at before entering Ihram, supplicating to Allah and asking for His help, saying: 'O Allah, I intend to perform Hajj, so facilitate it for me and release me from where You have bound me by Your decree that You have decreed upon me.' And say: 'My hair, skin, flesh, and blood are in Ihram for You, as are my women, garments, and perfume; I intend thereby Your Countenance and the Abode of the Hereafter, and release me from where You have bound me by Your decree that You have decreed upon me.' Then respond to the Call (Talbiyah) from Al-Masjid Al-Haram as you responded when you first entered Ihram, saying: 'Here I am, O Allah, with a Hajj whose completion and attainment are upon You.' If you are able, your departure to Mina should be at the time of the sun's decline (Zawal); otherwise, whenever it is convenient for you from the Day of Tarwiyah.

key_terms.اَلتَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tarwiyah, the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah
key_terms.اَلْمَسْجِدَ اَلْحَرَامَ: Al-Masjid Al-Haram (The Grand Mosque in Mecca)
key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: To enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.تُلَبِّي: To recite the Talbiyah (response to God's call)

ai.seo_question: What are the steps and supplications for entering Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* prescribes a comprehensive ritual protocol for entering Ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah, emphasizing physical purification (Ghusl, trimming hair and nails) and spiritual preparation through a six-Rak'at prayer in the Grand Mosque. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on specific supplications that acknowledge divine decree while seeking facilitation, and mandates the Talbiyah to be recited from the Masjid al-Haram, linking the pilgrim’s physical state directly to their spiritual intent for the Hereafter.
